rejected.title: What the Renaissance was
card: The Renaissance was a period in Europe when people revived the learning and art of ancient Greece and Rome. The word means rebirth.
It began in Italian cities in the 1300s and was flourishing in Florence by the 1400s. Later it spread to other parts of Europe.
Scholars read Greek and Roman writings again. Artists copied ancient ideas, such as lifelike human figures and balanced designs.
Europe in the Middle Ages had not forgotten the ancient world, but in the Renaissance interest in it grew strongly and shaped new work.
rejected.remember: The Renaissance was a rebirth of ancient Greek and Roman ideas and art, starting in Italian cities.

a.q: What was being reborn in the Renaissance?
opts: Greek and Roman learning and art
Medieval church rules and customs
The power of kings over their nobles
Trade routes between Europe and Asia
a.why: The word Renaissance means rebirth, and what was revived was the learning and art of ancient Greece and Rome. Medieval church customs were already part of life, so they were not being reborn.
a.clue: Think about which ancient peoples scholars and artists looked back to.

b.q: Marco is a scholar in Florence in the 1400s. He collects old Roman writings and copies their ideas into his own work. What does this show?
opts: The Renaissance revival of ancient learning
The end of interest in the ancient world
A new interest in learning from Asia
A spread of the Renaissance to Italy from Spain
b.why: Marco is reviving the learning of ancient Rome in Florence in the 1400s, when the Renaissance was flourishing there. The Renaissance began in Italy, so it did not spread to Italy from Spain.
b.clue: Look at where Marco lives, when, and what he is studying.
